sections.verb: The verb — where it comes from
sections.rulesHint: Tap any of them to open its full explanation right here.
sections.registers: The same sentence in three registers
sections.registersHint: One meaning, three social situations. They are not interchangeable.

verb.noStem: This verb is irregular — it isn't built from anything and has to be learned. Its full table is below, in the rule's explanation.

verbNotes.doubled-l: The l doubles in this form. Rule: wherever the ending is silent, the l doubles to keep the è sound — j'appelle but nous appelons.
verbNotes.memorised: Irregular. There is no stem-plus-ending pattern to follow; the whole table has to be learned, like English be: am, is, are.
verbNotes.silent-ending: The ending is silent. -e, -es and -ent all sound the same, so in speech only the pronoun tells you who is doing it.
verbNotes.fixed-expression: Part of a fixed expression, not conjugated on its own. il y a has one form for singular and plural, just like English there is / there are rolled into one.
verbNotes.politeness-form: This is the conditional, used to soften a request. je veux (I want) is correct but blunt; je voudrais (I would like) says the same thing politely.
verbNotes.stays-infinitive: This is the second verb, so it stays in the infinitive. When two verbs follow each other only the first is conjugated, like English I want to leave.
verbNotes.on-takes-3sg: on means we in everyday speech, but its verb is third person singular, like il. « on allons » is wrong.
verbNotes.impersonal-subject: The subject refers to nobody, like English it in « it is raining »; it is there only because French will not build a sentence without a subject.
verbNotes.noun-subject-is-3sg: The subject is a noun, not a pronoun — but the verb takes the third person singular, just as with il or elle.
verbNotes.participle-irregular: The past participle is irregular and has to be learned — it is not built from the infinitive, like English go → gone.
verbNotes.etre-verb: This verb takes être, not avoir, in the past. So the past participle agrees with the subject, like an adjective.
verbNotes.agreement-with-etre: Because the helper verb is être, the past participle agrees with the subject. You cannot hear it, but you must write it.
verbNotes.imperative-drops-s: In the tu form, -er verbs lose their s: tu parles but « Parle ! ».
verbNotes.imperative-no-subject: The imperative drops the subject pronoun, just as in English (Come!) — the only place French allows a verb without a subject.
verbNotes.impersonal-invariable: Never conjugated. It has a single form and its subject does not refer to anyone.
verbNotes.imparfait-from-nous: The stem comes from the present nous form (nous parl-ons → parl-) and the endings are the same for every verb: ais · ais · ait · ions · iez · aient. The only exception is être: ét-.
verbNotes.futur-from-infinitive: The stem is the infinitive itself (-re verbs drop the final e) and the endings are the present of avoir: ai · as · a · ons · ez · ont.
verbNotes.futur-stem-irregular: Its future stem is irregular and has to be learned; the endings are the usual ones: ai · as · a · ons · ez · ont.
verbNotes.subjonctif-from-ils: The stem comes from the present ils form (ils partent → part-) and the endings are: e · es · e · ions · iez · ent.
verbNotes.pronominal-etre: A reflexive verb always takes être in the past, and the past participle agrees with the subject.
verbNotes.advice-form: Conditional used for advice: tu dois = you must (an order), tu devrais = you should (advice). The stem is the future stem (devr-) and the endings are those of the imparfait.
verbNotes.recent-past: venir is in the present but the meaning is the recent past: venir de + infinitive = to have just done something.

verdictWrongDetail: This isn't the sentence this card wanted. If what you wrote is correct French, it isn't wrong — this card was just looking for the form below. See the differences:

finished.title: {{level}} complete
finished.body: You have seen every sentence at this level. Go round again — nothing is deleted, it just starts over.
finished.unitBody: You have seen every sentence in this unit. The level goes on — the course picks up at the next one.
finished.topicBody: You have seen every sentence on this topic at this level. Lift the filter and the rest of the level is there.

listen.textStep: Now read it — what does it mean?
listen.askHeard: Before you saw the text, had you caught the words?
listen.missedIt: No, I only got it from the text
listen.earAgain: You didn't catch it by ear — it comes back soon for listening practice.
listen.askHeardHint: Getting it now that you see the text doesn't count; what matters is the moment you heard it.

settings.title: Settings
settings.autoPlayHint: The sentence is read aloud as it appears — in writing mode, once you have seen the answer.
settings.mixHint: Every few cards, a sentence that is due for review takes the place of a new one. With this off, the round runs exactly as you set it.

review.empty: Nothing to review right now. Any sentence you get wrong comes back here a few minutes later.

schedule.again: This one comes back in a few minutes, and keeps coming back until you get it right.
schedule.later: Correct — you'll see it again in {{days}} days.
schedule.learned: You know this one now. We'll ask once more in {{days}} days so it sticks.

history.title: Your sentence practice record
history.subtitle: Sentences you've answered — which ones you know and which ones will come back.

empty.learned: You haven't got a sentence right twice in a row yet — the second correct answer marks it «known».
empty.all: You haven't answered any sentences yet.
empty.misheard: No sentences left that your ear missed.

askKnewHint: Be your own judge: before you saw the meaning, did you already have this in mind?
liaisonHint: These two words run together and are said in one breath (liaison).

qa.step: Read the question and write your answer
qa.heard: Had you caught the question by ear?
qa.slotsHint: Use your own name, numbers and city.

grade.unmatched: Doesn't match the model answers — compare and judge for yourself

qa.askRightHint: Compare it with the answers above. If it means the right thing and the French is sound, it's right — even if it isn't word for word.

meaning.pass: It says what the card asked for.
meaning.fail: It doesn't say what the card asked for.

elision.fail: An elision is missing — a word that must contract was written out in full (for example me aider instead of m'aider).

register.formal: Formal register — right for a letter or a stranger.
register.informal: Informal register — perfect for a text to a friend.

natural.yes: Sounds natural — a native speaker would say it this way.
natural.no: Correct, but a native speaker would put it differently.

error.gender_agreement: Looks like a gender or number agreement slip.
error.verb_conjugation: Check the verb's form or tense.
error.wrong_word: One word doesn't fit the meaning.
error.avoir_expression: French says avoir here, not être: j'ai faim, quel âge avez-vous ?

retry.title: You wrote this one wrong — write it again
retry.hint: It came back because it missed. Write it correctly once to move on. You can skip it for now — but the next time it comes back, skipping will not be on offer.
retry.lockedTitle: You have written this one wrong {{count}} times
retry.lockedHint: You skipped it last time. This time, write it correctly to move on.

desk.aiFallback: Your AI could not check this one, so the card's own check decided.
